newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks fall 4 pct on shattered reform hopes.
newsitem.headline: India stocks fall 4 pct on shattered reform hopes.

text.p: Indian shares tumbled more than four percent on Friday as nervous traders offloaded blue chips after an eagerly awaited market reform package failed to materialise.
In afternoon trade, the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index plunged 148.80 points, or 4.24 percent, to 3,361.25 in a session traders described as "nerve-wracking".
By the day's close, it had lost 130.30 points, or 3.7 percent, to end at a provisional 3,379.75.

Traders' hopes for a new package of policy initiatives that would boost the capital markets collapsed after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said late on Thursday that it was actually made up of a series of measures announced in January.

"We have seen the initial break down. Everyone seems to be waiting for the others to react...There's more confusion than anything else," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at foreign brokerage James Capel B&K.

Last Monday, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said the government would announce new economic measures before he departed with Chidambaram for the World Economic Forum summit at Davos in Switzerland on Friday.
But traders were disappointed by the actual announcement.
"It's very irresponsible on the part of the prime minister," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
The reforms Chidambaram referred to included decisions to permit foreign portfolio investment in debt and government bonds, as well as boosting investment in infrastructure.
They constituted a cohesive package of decisions which would impart greater thrust to the economic reforms, Chidambaram said.
"It's a big disappointment," said Capel's Sanghvi.
Moves by the Securities and Exchange Board of India to open the debt market to foreign investors were seen as positive, but traders said the measures were too little, too late.
"People are losing confidence in the government. The prime minister had repeatedly promised to announce a package in January," lamented K.R. Choksey, a member-broker of the BSE.
"Investors are bound to refrain from entering the market," he said.
Lingering hopes of new government announcements on Friday were finally put to rest after the Finance Ministry confirmed that Deve Gowda and Chidambaram had left for Davos.
The Bombay share index surged 24 percent in the New Year on hopes for a new package.
"The sentiment has definitely turned bearish. People who had built up long positions are offloading," said Govind Agarwal, a dealer at Motilal Oswal, a local brokerage.
